courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Introduction to Optical Communications
courses.description: This course covers the physics, technology, and engineering applications of optical communications. The topics include overview on the development of fiber communications, optical fibers and their properties, LED and Laser sources, optical power launching and coupling, optical detectors and receivers, repeaters, regenerators, and optical amplifiers, introduction to optical communication systems, modulation and multiplexing technologies, optical networks, and nonlinear fiber optics. Recent developments in optical communication technology will also be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken ELEG3320 or ESTR3206.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should be able to:
- obtain an overall picture of the history, progress, and importance of optical communications, and understand its advantages and limitations.
- understand the physical principle and technology of different components in an optical communication system, including optical transmitter, optical fiber, signal regenerator, optical amplifier, and optical receiver.
- perform quantitative analysis of optical components and system performance.
- understand different technologies used in optical communications (such as signal modulation and multiplexing) and their importance.
- safely handle optical fibers and perform simple optical experiments
courses.course_syllabus: Overview on the development of fiber communications, optical fibers and their properties, LED and Laser sources, optical power launching and coupling, optical detectors and receivers, repeaters, regenerators, and optical amplifiers, introduction to optical communication systems, modulation and multiplexing technologies, optical networks, and nonlinear fiber optics; Recent developments in optical communication technology.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits Design
courses.description: This course reviews the transistor and wire characteristics and models in modern digital CMOS technologies. Performance metrics for digital circuits are introduced. Design and optimization of various types of digital integrated circuits are discussed. They include static combinational logic circuits, dynamic combinational logic circuits, and sequential logic circuits. An exemplary arithmetic circuit is studied. The course also covers the design of memory and array structures, noise in digital systems, I/O and signaling conventions.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken ELEG4201 or ELEG4260
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon satisfactory completion of this course, the students will be able to:
- Demonstrate an understanding of devices used in modern CMOS digital ICs.
- Demonstrate an ability to describe the performance metrics of CMOS digital ICs.
- Demonstrate an ability to analyse the performance of digital integrated circuits: static and dynamic combination logic, sequential logic and memory.
- Demonstrate an ability to design digital integrated circuits: static and dynamic combination logic, sequential logic and memory.
- Demonstrate the ability to design and verify digital circuits using an design automation tool
courses.course_syllabus: This course reviews the transistor and wire characteristics and models in modern digital CMOS technologies. Performance metrics for digital circuits are introduced. Design and optimization of various types of digital integrated circuits are discussed. They include static combinational logic circuits, dynamic combinational logic circuits, and sequential logic circuits. An exemplary arithmetic circuit is studied. The course also covers the design of memory and array structures, noise in digital systems, I/O and signaling conventions.

courses.title: Design Methodology of Modern Digital Circuits
courses.description: This course teaches the design methods for modern digital circuits. Digital circuit technology trends are described. Implementation methods and design flows for modern digital circuits are explained in detail, and their trade-offs are discussed. Advanced circuit techniques in digital designs are introduced. Design tools, e.g., Verilog, are taught. Packaging and testing of digital integrated circuits are briefed.

- understand the intricate trade-offs in different implementation methods
- know with design flows and have the competence to use design tools
- use Verilog as a Hardware Description Language
- apply advanced circuit techniques in digital designs
- gain a comprehensive knowledge of integrated circuits as a technology
- gain hands-on experience in implementing digital designs into hardware through practice

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Physics and Technology of Semiconductor Devices
courses.description: This is an elective course for ELEG undergraduate students who are interested in the physics and technology of semiconductor devices. The course content is designed to equip the students with the fundamental concepts and principles of the semiconductor devices. It will discuss advanced physical mechanisms which limit the performance of state-of-the-art diodes and transistors. The course begins with the basic knowledge about the semiconductors, and is then advanced to the fundamental physics and principles of the semiconductor devices. Finally, the course connects the design and fabrication of semiconductor devices and circuits to the material and device physics. The course will also be extended to novel semiconductor technologies such as flexible and wearable electronics.

Prerequisites: ELEG3301 or ESTR3204 or consent of the instructor.

1. Fundament of semiconductors physics

2. PN junction, Metal-Semiconductor contacts, Metal-Insulator-Semiconductor

3. Bipolar transistors

4. MOS field-effect transistors

5. CMOS circuits

6. Optoelectronics, such as photodetectors, light-emitting diodes and lasers

7. Semiconductor manufacturing

8. Flexible electronics

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Processing of Functional Materials
courses.description: The processing techniques used to manufacture materials and components is a very broad activity encompassing materials science, mechanical engineering, electronic engineering, chemistry and economics. Commercial processing is now accomplished by automated and computer controlled equipment yet the engineers and researchers must understand the basic principles to program and control the parameters. This course is to develop the scientific base and fundamental nature of some common processes. The aim of this course is to provide students with the basic understanding of manufacturing processes, and the relationships between process design and fundamental concepts in transport phenomena, and properties.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For ELEG RPG & TPG students
courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of this course the students will be able to

1. **Explain** the relationships between basic concepts and design of the processing route.
2. **Apply** basic concepts to predict the material behaviour during processing.
3. **Predict** the structure and properties of the end products
4. **List** the advantages and limitations of each process
5. **Choose** the best process for a particular component, device or material.
courses.course_syllabus:
The following topics will be covered:

* *Module 1 : Processes for Particulate Materials and bulk materials**

* *a: Powder synthesis and bulk fabrication process**

Methods for powder production and blending. Particle shape and size distribution. Properties of powders.

* *b: Compaction of Powders**

Young’s Laplace equations, Kevin equations, Sintering and mechanisms, liquid sintering, solid sintering, Various densities. Pressing. Isostatic pressing. cermets and composite. Properties of sintered products.

* *Module 2: Vacuum Processes**

* *a: Vacuum**

Introduction to UHV technology, systems, pumps and gauges. Units of pressure. Deposition chambers, target and substrate preparation.

* *b: Fabrication process and structural characterizations**

Physical vapour deposition processes and sputtering. Polycrystalline and epitaxial film production. Effects of substrates; Chemical Vapor Deposition, Films and nanostructures from gas precursors. Atomic layer deposition. Nanoscale control of film chemistry. Epitaxial layer characterization. Reciprocal lattice map. Quantify the defects in the films.

* *c. Growth progress and Microstructure control**

Zone structure model, amorphous and crystallinity control, pore control and defects evolutions

Volmer-Weber, layer Stranski-Krastanov growth, Growth of quantum dots. Structure modification. Amorphous films. Adhesion. Stress evolution. Measurement of stress. Controlling stress.

* *Module 3: Solution Processes**

* *a: Basic Principles**

Precursor solutions, reaction rates, ligand additives for size and shape control.

* *b:Sol Gel**

The principal of Sol gel and the related process. Morphology control, Chemical reaction of sol gel, the advantages and disadvantages of sol gels. Basics of sol-gel,

* *c: Chemical Solution Deposition — Basic Principles**

chelate and related processes. Film formation: spin coating, dip coating and spray coating. Spray pyrolysis. Examples of chemical synthesis. Examples of chalcogenide semiconductor synthesis. Processing of polymer, and hybrid materials.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Audio Signal Processing
courses.description: This course is an in-depth exploration of audio processing using neural networks. Starting with an introduction to audio problems, the course covers a range of topics including audio features and human labels, filtering and digital signal processing for audio processing, audio and music tagging with convolutional neural networks, audio and music transcription with recurrent neural networks, audio compression, bridging audio and language with sequence-to-sequence models, symbolic music generation, audio and music generation with pipelines, vocoder, and autoregressive models, audio and music generation with VAEs and diffusion models, controllable audio and music generation from texts and multiple modalities, and open problems and future directions in the field.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For ELEG PG students; For ELEG UG major and minor as elective. Students should have knowledge of Linear Algebra, Probability, C/C++/Python, pattern recognition or machine learning. UG students should have taken ENGG1120, ENGG2760, CSCI1120 or equivalent.
courses.learning_outcomes: Through a combination of lectures, assignments, and projects, students will gain hands-on experience working with state-of-the-art tools and techniques for audio and music processing. By the end of the course, students will have a solid foundation in the latest techniques for audio and music processing using neural networks, and will be able to apply these techniques to real-world problems in the field.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Introduction: Audio and music problems.
2. Audio features and human labels.
3. Filtering, digital signal processing for audio processing (Assignment 1)
4. Audio and music tagging with convolutional neural networks.
5. Audio and music transcription with recurrent neural networks.
6. Audio compression.
7. Bridging audio and language: audio and music caption with sequence-to-sequence models (Assignment 2).
8. Symbolic music generation.
9. Audio and music generation: pipelines, vocoder, and autoregressive models.
10. Audio and music generation with probabilistic models, such as diffusion models.
11. Controllable audio and music generation from texts and multiple modalities (Assignment 3).
12. Open problems and future.

courses.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to deep learning. Students taking this course will learn the theories, models, algorithms, implementation and recent progress of deep learning, and obtain empirical experience on training deep neural networks. The course starts with machine learning basics and some classical deep models (including convolutional neural network, deep belief net, and auto-encoder), followed by optimization techniques for training deep neural networks, implementation of large-scale deep learning, multi-task deep learning, transferred deep learning, recurrent neural networks, applications of deep learning to computer vision and speech recognition, and understanding why deep learning works. The students taking are expected to have some basic background knowledge on calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and random process as a prerequisite.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For ELEG RPG & TPG students, ELEG undergraduate major and minor students as elective course; Not for students who have taken ELEG5040
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand the fundamental concepts, theories and algorithms of deep learning.
2. Understand why deep learning outperforms other machine learning methods when the training data is in large scale
3. Understand the principles of designing different deep models for various applications
4. Implement and train deep neural networks with deep learning toolboxes
5. Obtain empirical experience of designing and training deep models in practical applications.
courses.course_syllabus: This course provides an introduction to deep learning. Students taking this course will learn the theories, models, algorithms, implementation and recent progress of deep learning, and obtain empirical experience on training deep neural networks. The course starts with machine learning basics and some classical deep models (including convolutional neural network, deep belief net, and auto-encoder), followed by optimization techniques for training deep neural networks, implementation of large-scale deep learning, multi-task deep learning, transferred deep learning, recurrent neural networks, applications of deep learning to computer vision and speech recognition, and understanding why deep learning works. The students taking are expected to have some basic background knowledge on calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and random process as a prerequisite.
courses.feedback_evaluation:
We welcome students’ comments and feedback on the course. There are five main channels for collecting students’ feedback.
1. Mid-term tests: They help teacher understand how much students have understood the course materials.
2. Tutorial and lectures: Students are encouraged to ask questions during lectures. They can also pass their feedback and problems about the course to teaching assistants or to the teachers directly.
3. Informal online contact: Students can write their comments via emails or newsgroup. Teaching assistants will follow up with the comments on newsgroup and pass the information to the teacher if necessary.
4. Individual consulting: Students are welcome to contact the teacher during office hours. However, as students are practicing engineers, so such contact is not many.
5. Faculty course questionnaire: At the end of the course, students are required to provide feedback on different aspects related to teaching and learning of the course through a formal evaluation questionnaire.
courses.required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
courses.recommended_readings:
1. Y. Bengio, I. Goodfellow, and A. Courville, “Deep Learning,” Book in preparation for MIT press.
2. Y. Bengio, “Learning Deep Architectures for AI,” Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning, 2009.

courses.title: Advanced Perception for Intelligent Robotics
courses.description: This course introduces the advanced topics in perception for intelligent robotics. It covers fundamental concepts and techniques of machine vision, robotic image and video processing, sensor fusion for semantic mapping and exploration, pattern recognition, learning and deep neural networks, robotic scenario intelligence, perception and anticipation of human behaviors, and advanced robotic trajectory and task planning. Case studies of successful medical and service robotics are discussed. In the course project, students are required to propose, design and implement a robotic system with intelligent perception to map and explore dynamic environment and interact with human subjects.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Electronic Engineering Seminar
courses.description: Electronic engineering is a fast evolving interdisciplinary field. This course consists of the most up-to-date research topics presented by active researchers and experts in the field and strikes a balance between discussions of hardware and software development in electronic engineering. There will be 26 seminars in total, and each seminar contains a 45-minute presentation followed by a 25-minute discussion session. The students are required to attend at least 70% of the seminars and write one report on their learning from one or two specific seminars.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to

1. Stay abreast of latest technological developments in the field of electronic engineering
2. Acquire knowledge of research topics related to electronic engineering
3. Acquire, enhance, and practice presentation skills
4. Develop skills in analytical and reflective thinking
courses.course_syllabus: Seminars in the areas of image and video processing, digital signal processing and speech technology, microwave and wireless communications, robotics, perception and AI, photonics and optical communications, solid state electronics and VLSI, ASIC and energy conversion.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Optical Communications and Interconnects
courses.description: This course provides an overview of optical fibre communications. The course content includes types and properties of fibres, optical transmitters, receivers, and repeaters, passive optical devices, optical modulation and multiplexing techniques, fibre communication systems and optical networks. The course also introduces optical interconnects, silicon photonics, active optical cables and discusses future trends of optical interconnects.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg and MSc Electronic Engineering
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should obtain an overall picture of the history and recent developments of optical communications, and understand its advantages and limitations. They will acquire knowledge on the operating principle and technology of different key components in an optical communication system and optical interconnects. They should be able to apply skills for the design of basic fibre components, systems, and networks and carry out qualitative and quantitative analyses on their performances.
courses.course_syllabus: Introduction to optical interconnects. Silicon photonics: waveguides, grating couplers, directional couplers, multimode interferometers, nonlinear and electro-optic effects; Overview of optical fibre communications. Types and properties of fibres. Optical transmitters, receivers, and repeaters. Passive optical component. Optical modulation and multiplexing techniques. Fibre communication systems. Optical networks. Silicon modulators and optical receivers. Recent trends.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: VLSI Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: This course deals with the methodologies of designing VLSI circuits for DSP algorithms for a wide range of applications. It introduces architectural techniques to optimize for speed, power consumption or size, e.g., pipelining, retiming, unfolding, folding and systolic array. The course also teaches hardware description language (HDL), and shows examples of using HDL to design signal processing systems. Practical work will be arranged for students to gain hand-on experience of designing and implementation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Electronic Engineering
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Use signal diagram to describe digital signal processing algorithms.
2. Understand different architectural transforms to optimize a VLSI DSP circuit for speed, power consumption or size.
3. Understand a Hardware Description Language and has the ability to use the HDL to design VLSI DSP circuits.
4. Gain the experience of using FPGA Design Tools.
courses.course_syllabus: This course deals with methodologies to design VLSI circuits for DSP algorithms used in a wide range of signal processing applications. Architectural techniques to optimize for speed, power consumption or size include pipelining, retiming, unfolding, folding and systolic array. The course also introduces a hardware description language, and shows the use of HDL to design a specific digital processing example. Practical will be arranged for students to gain first hand experience of designing and implementing DSP algorithms.
courses.required_readings: To be provided by the course teacher.
courses.recommended_readings:

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Processor Design with RISC-V
courses.description: RISC-V is the processor of choice after Intel x86 and ARM processor. RISC-V is an open core and is fully configurable to support a wide scope of applications with varying performance requirements. This course will cover basic processor design. RISC-V instruction set architecture will be described along with an elementary pipelined implementation. Based on the elementary design, different techniques to increase performance will be examined from different levels of cache to instruction level and data level parallelism.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg and MSc Electronic Engineering
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand the basic concept of processor design
2. Understand RISC-V ISA and appreciate the merit of different control implementations
3. Use memory organization to increase performance
4. Use different levels of parallelism to increase performance
5. Gain ability to configure a RISC-V

Data Level Parallelism

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence IC Design
courses.description:
With the rapid development and increasingly application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology, specific AI Integrated Circuits (IC) are required to provide powerful and efficient computing capability, which drives the needs in market for types of AI IC suitable for different application situation. Therefore, this course intends to provide the enrolled students with the typical technology, system architecture and design methodology for AI IC design. Moreover, software tool chains are also introduced. This course is to support and enable the students with improved capability to design AI IC.
The content of this course is composed of five sections: 1) Fundamentals of AI and typical algorithms; 2) Technology and system architecture of AI IC, as well as design methodology considering algorithm, software and hardware; 3) Software tool chains related to the application of AI IC; 4) Emerging semiconductor devices, computing modality, circuit design, system architecture, requirement and trend; 5) Practice of AI IC design. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with essential knowledge in AI algorithm, software and IC design.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Electronic Engineering and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. Understand the introductory knowledge and typical algorithms of AI computing.

2. Understand the typical techniques and representative architectures of AI IC.

3. Understand the Domain-Specific Architecture (DSA) design methodology including algorithm, hardware and software.

4. Understand the software tools for the application of AI IC.

5. Understand emerging semiconductor devices, system architecture, requirement and trend.

6. Obtain practical experience of system development including requirement analysis, algorithm optimization, IC architecture and module design.

Fundamentals of AI algorithms

Architectures of AI IC – Overview

Architectures of AI IC – Operator

Emerging devices, architectures and trend

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Fundamentals of Automotive Integrated Circuits
courses.description:
The emerging intelligence of automotive vehicles requires increasingly powerful computing capability embedded on vehicle, which motivates the eager demand for automotive Integrated Circuit (IC). Because of such specifics as high reliability, the automotive IC is quite distinct from consumer IC. This course intends to provide for the enrolled students with the knowledge of automotive IC, including the characteristics, fabrication process, development flow, testing, packaging, related software and application. The students can therefore be with fundamental knowledge and development capability of automotive IC.
The content of this course is composed of six parts: 1) Overview and particulars of automotive IC; 2) Fabrication process and devices of automotive IC; 3) Design of analog automotive IC; 4) Design of digital automotive IC; 5) Testing and packaging of automotive IC; 6) Software related to automotive IC. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge in physics, software and integrated circuits.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Electronic Engineering and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Understand the basic knowledge and particulars of automotive IC.
2. Understand the fabrication techniques and devices for automotive IC.
3. Understand the fundamental design techniques for analog and digital automotive IC.
4. Understand the knowledge about the testing and packaging of automotive IC.
5. Understand the software related to automotive IC.
6. Obtain practical experience of designing automotive IC.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: AI in Medical Image Analysis
courses.description:
Medical imaging has been an integral part in modern healthcare procedures. Advances in deep learning have revolutionized the analysis of biomedical data, clinical diagnosis, and prognosis. In this course, students will learn fundamental image processing techniques, characteristics of different types of medical images, and how to apply different classical image processing techniques to different types of medical images. Topics covered in this course include but are not limited to:
- An overview of medical imaging modalities and their clinical use,
- Introduction to medical image computing, including registration, segmentation, classification, reconstruction, super-resolution, and visualization,
- Traditional image processing techniques for medical image analysis,
- Machine learning/deep learning for medical image analysis, and
- Frontline of AI in medical imaging and case studies.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: CMOS Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits Design
courses.description:
This subject aims to train students with the advanced knowledge of radio frequency (RF) integrated circuit design in the advanced CMOS technology, including design and analysis of widely-used RF transceiver architectures and circuits. The student will get hands-on experience to design and analyze RF integrated circuits and get familiar with the complete design flow from circuit design, layout design and parasitic parameters extraction.

The content of this course is composed of seven parts: 1)RF passive circuits and matching networks; 2) Noise and nonlinearity in RF system; 3) Communication system and standard; 4) RF transceiver architecture; 5) RF transceiver calibration; 6) RF module circuit design; 7) Introduction to mmWave IC. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge in physics, semiconductor device and integrated circuits.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Electronic Engineering
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. Understand RFIC system and architecture design.
2. Understand popular communication system and standard.
3. Analyze important RF module circuits in advanced CMOS process.
4. Use mainstream EDA tools in the industry to design and optimize the performance of RF module circuits.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Mixed-signal Integrated Circuit Design
courses.description:
This subject aims to train students with the advanced knowledge of mixed-signal integrated circuit design in the advanced CMOS technology, including design and analysis of the circuit and theory of switch capacitor circuit, analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and digital-to-analog converter (DAC). The student will get hands-on experience to design and analyze advanced mixed-signal integrated circuits and complete design flow from circuit design, layout design and parasitic parameters extraction.

The content of this course is composed of eight parts: 1) ADC/DAC fundamentals; 2) switch capacitor circuit; 3) SAR ADC; 4) pipelined ADC; 5) interleaved ADC; 6) sigma-delta ADC; 7) high resolution DAC; 8) high-speed DAC. The students to be enrolled in this course are required to be with basic knowledge in physics, semiconductor device and integrated circuits.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Electronic Engineering
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. Understand the advanced knowledge of mixed-signal IC design in CMOS process.

2. Understand the switch capacitor circuit design.

3. Analyze important ADC design including SAR ADC, pipelined ADC, interleaved ADC and sigma-delta ADC.

4. Analyze important DAC design including current steering DAC, R-2R DAC and sigma-delta DAC.

5. Use mainstream EDA tools in the industry to optimize the performance mixed-signal integrated circuits.

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Advanced Semiconductor Packaging
courses.description:
This subject aims to train students with the fundamental knowledge of microelectronic and power electronic packaging technologies, including concepts, electrical design, structural & thermal design, material selection, process development, test and failure analysis, with the focus on the understanding of mainstream packaging technologies for high-power & high-frequency related applications. Tutorials can be arranged to ensure the students with hand-on experience on the mainstream design software and understand the fabrication process of electronic packages/modules in industry.
The content of this course is composed of seven parts: 1) Mainstream microelectronics packaging format & process; 2) Mainstream power electronics packaging format & process; 3) Fundamentals of thermal management, mechanics & reliability; 4) Electrical, thermal and mechanical co-design considerations with case studies; 5) Modelling and simulation of mainstream electronic packages; 6) Chiplet design and heterogeneous integration packaging; 7) Techniques for failure analysis.

Fundamental of mechanics & reliability II

Modelling & simulation of electronic packages II

Emerging power packaging technology and process
Chiplet design and heterogeneous integration packaging
Failure analysis

courses.subject: ELEG
courses.title: Photonic Chip Design and Emerging Applications
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the principles, techniques, and cutting-edge developments in photonic chip design. The course covers fundamental concepts in waveguide theory, optical materials, devices, circuits and simulation methodologies used in photonic integrated circuit (PIC) design. Beyond the fundamentals, the course introduces a wide range of emerging applications, including ultrafast optical communication, optical computing, sensing, and quantum photonics. Students will understand the theoretical foundations and the real-world opportunities of photonic chip technologies, preparing them for advanced study or careers in integrated photonics and semiconductor technology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Electronic Engineering and MPhil-PhD Electronic Erg;Not for students who have taken ELEG5301
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand fundamental physics of waveguides, optical materials, and photonic device structures used in photonic integrated circuits (PICs).

2. Design basic photonic components and circuits using industry-standard simulation tools and evaluate their performance.

3. Understand the fundamental principles of photonic chip manufacturing

4. Understand the principle and assessment of emerging applications of photonic chips, including ultrafast optical communication, optical computing, sensing, and quantum photonics.
courses.course_syllabus:
Introduction to photonic integrated circuits

Fundamentals of waveguides

Passive optical devices

Active optical devices

Simulation and design tools

Manufacturing technology

Photonic circuits & system-level design

Applications of photonic integrated circuits

Emerging trends and future technologies
